learning_outcomes.text: Students will learn to set up complex mass balances in single/multiple, reactive/non-reactive systems.
Students will determine appropriate parameters using "Degree of Freedom Analysis" for cases where calculations cannot be performed manually before computer simulation.
Students will learn to construct computer solutions for algebraic equations.
Students will learn sequential modular simulation and equation-based simulation techniques.
Case studies will be applied in class to create a process for degree of freedom analysis and solve this process using a computer-based calculation.

syllabus_topics: Advanced Mass Balances: General Mass Balance Equation, Multiple Units, Stoichiometry, Degree of Freedom Analysis, Gibbs Phase Rule
Advanced Excel Applications Classwork 1: Using the SRK Equation Classwork 2: Bubble and Dew Point Calculations
Mass and Energy Balances In-Class Work 3: Energy Balance in a Waste Heat Boiler In-Class Work 4: Energy Balance in an Adiabatic Reactor
Review of Degree of Freedom Analysis Classwork 5: Flash Evaporator
Degree of Freedom Analysis in Multiple Units Solution of Algebraic Equations
Sequential Modular Simulation: Elements of Modular Simulation Classwork 6: Structure of a Mixing Block Routine
Simulation of Acrylic Acid Process, Cyclic Systems and Convergence Block Classwork 7: Simulation of a Cyclic Process
Equation Based Simulation Classwork 8: Simulation and Design of a Two-Column Separation Process
Classwork 9: Simulation of an Equilibrium Reaction / Separation Process
Simulation of an Ammonium Nitride Plant
